events.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
events.description: According to the traditional date, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under volcanic ash and pumice, killing thousands of residents. Recent archaeological evidence suggests the eruption may have occurred later in the autumn.
events.significance: The eruption preserved Pompeii and Herculaneum almost intact, giving historians and archaeologists an unparalleled window into daily life in the Roman Empire and founding the modern study of volcanology.

events.title: St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre Begins
events.description: In Paris, Catholic mobs and soldiers began killing French Huguenots (Protestants) days after the wedding of Henry of Navarre and Margaret of Valois. The violence spread to other French cities and continued for weeks, killing thousands.
events.significance: The massacre deepened the French Wars of Religion and became a lasting symbol of religious intolerance and the dangers of sectarian conflict in Europe.

events.title: British Burn Washington, D.C.
events.description: During the War of 1812, British forces defeated American troops at the Battle of Bladensburg and entered Washington, D.C., burning the Capitol, the White House, and other public buildings in retaliation for the American burning of York (Toronto) in 1813.
events.significance: It was the only time a foreign power has captured and occupied the U.S. capital, and the event spurred American resolve that contributed to the successful defense of Baltimore and the writing of The Star-Spangled Banner.

events.title: Ukraine Declares Independence from the Soviet Union
events.description: Following the failed hardline coup in Moscow, the Ukrainian parliament adopted the Act of Independence of Ukraine, declaring the country independent of the USSR. A national referendum on December 1 overwhelmingly confirmed it.
events.significance: Ukraine's independence was a decisive step in the dissolution of the Soviet Union, which formally ended in December 1991, and reshaped the political map of Eastern Europe.

events.title: Pluto Reclassified as a Dwarf Planet
events.description: The International Astronomical Union voted at its General Assembly in Prague to adopt a formal definition of a planet, which excluded Pluto and reclassified it as a dwarf planet.
events.significance: The decision changed the official count of planets in the Solar System from nine to eight and sparked widespread public debate about how scientific categories are defined.
